action: Slide the probe up and down the thorax. Interrogate multiple intercostal spaces.
interpretation: Scan the thoracic region to assess lung sliding and artifacts.

action: Focus attention on the top of the screen.
interpretation: Identify the pleural line. Note that the pleural line is shimmering.
Optimize settings to visualize motion and the pleural interface more clearly.

action: Verify the presence of shimmering at the pleural line.
interpretation: Confirm clear shimmering. Conclude that there is no pneumothorax.
Observe horizontal lines indicating the lung is air-filled in this area. Use this finding to rule out pneumonia or effusion.

action: Drag the probe inferiorly towards the base of the lung. Locate the diaphragm.
interpretation: Transition the view from the upper intercostal spaces to the lung base.
Adjust image parameters to optimize the view of the lung base structures.

action: Hold position at the lung base. Visualize the anatomical landmarks.
interpretation: Identify the liver, the kidney, and the spine at the bottom of the screen. Identify the diaphragm as the diagonal hyperechoic line.

action: Assess the image for mirror image artifact.
interpretation: Observe the liver reflecting over the diaphragm into the thorax.

action: Correlate the artifact with lung pathology status.
interpretation: Recognize that the mirror image artifact indicates the lung is air-filled. Confirm this is a normal lung finding.

action: Conclude the assessment of the right lung base.
interpretation: Determine that the patient has no effusion or pneumonia at the right base of the lung.
